newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner bids for S. America bridge - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner bids for S. America bridge - paper.

text.p: Engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA is one of 20 international companies bidding to build the world's largest bridge in South America, the Norwegian daily Arbeiderbladet said on Wednesday.
The bridge is planned to span between Punta Lara in Argentina and Colonia in Uruguay over the Rio de la Plata, the newspaper said.

Preliminary estimates put the cost of the structure at around seven billion crowns. The company that wins the project will get a return on its investment in 35 years via road tolls, the Arbeiderbladet said.
Trond Andresen, spokesman at Kvaerner's headquarters in London, said he was not aware of the project.
"It must be in the very preliminary stages," Andresen told Reuters. "But we have built most of the largest bridges in the world. If this is planned then we will be in the picture."
Kvaerner will shortly finish the Tsing Ma structure, the world's largest suspension bridge, in Hong Kong, and recently won a contract in China for the Ying Jan bridge over the Yangtze River.
